newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan rose slightly on Tuesday on expectations of a rise in China's November trade surplus, ending at 8.2992 against the U.S. dollar from Monday's 8.2999 in the interbank foreign exchange market, traders said.
The yuan opened slightly higher at 8.2996 and consolidated between an intra-day high of 8.2991 and a low of 8.2998 for most of the session.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2996, traders said.
Dealers said China's trade figures, due to be announced at the weekend, are likely to show an increased surplus, which pushed up the yuan.
"But thin volume and a narrow range of trading limited the rise of the yuan," said a second dealer.
"No matter how the yuan moves, it will not be far from the 8.3000 level for the rest of this year," he added.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.3000 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed up at an intra-day high of 7.3000 from 7.3700 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly down at 1.0744 from 1.0740 against the Hong Kong dollar.
